purpose: Summative performance task for the full unit. Each child plans a rule, builds an animal parade, translates it to a number parade using whole numbers up to 50, and justifies the rule. Used as primary summative evidence for C1.1, C1.2, C1.3, and C1.4.
student_learning_goal: I can build a repeating number parade up to 50, name its rule, and lead it.

parts.answer_key: My Rule box: any valid rule label (AB, ABB, AAB, or ABC). Children who invent a new rule (ABCB, AABB) are accepted — note for L4 evidence on C1.3. My Core box: a small drawing of the core that matches the rule (e.g., for AAB: two of the same animal followed by one different). The loop is drawn around the core. The rule and the core must match — a child writing 'ABB' in My Rule and drawing AB in My Core needs a conference.

Footprints beneath the strip. To the side of the strip, the four-animal key reprinted as a quick reference.

parts.answer_key: An 8-cell parade following the rule the child wrote in Part 1. Loop drawn around the first core. Examples: Rule AB → Bea-Finn-Bea-Finn-Bea-Finn-Bea-Finn (loop around cells 1–2). Rule ABB → Bea-Finn-Finn-Bea-Finn-Finn-Bea-Finn (loop around cells 1–3). Rule AAB → Bea-Bea-Finn-Bea-Bea-Finn-Bea-Bea (loop around cells 1–3). Rule ABC → Bea-Finn-Bibi-Bea-Finn-Bibi-Bea-Finn (loop around cells 1–3). Correct if the child's parade follows their rule consistently across all 8 cells AND the loop frames a valid core.

parts.part_title: Part 3: Translate to a number parade up to 50

parts.answer_key: Two or three numbers between 1 and 50 written in the key (A and B always; C only if rule is ABC). 8-cell number parade following the same rule as the animal parade in Part 2. Examples: Rule AB with A=10, B=25 → 10-25-10-25-10-25-10-25. Rule ABB with A=4, B=12 → 4-12-12-4-12-12-4-12. Rule AAB with A=2, B=50 → 2-2-50-2-2-50-2-2. Rule ABC with A=5, B=15, C=30 → 5-15-30-5-15-30-5-15. Correct if the rule from Part 2 is preserved AND the chosen numbers are between 1 and 50. The justify sentence at the bottom: any reasonable explanation referencing the rule (e.g., 'My rule works because A is 10 and B is 25 and the rule AB means they take turns').

early_finisher_prompt: If you finish, flip the page over and draw what cell 9 and cell 10 would look like in your number parade. Could you predict cell 20?
teacher_notes: SUMMATIVE worksheet — the most important artifact in the unit. Score each completed worksheet against the 4-level rubric (see assessment_suite). Look for: (1) Did the rule and core match in Part 1? — C1.3 evidence. (2) Did the 8 animal cells follow the rule? — C1.1 evidence. (3) Did the number parade preserve the rule with valid numbers 1–50? — C1.4 + C1.2 evidence. (4) Did the justify sentence reference the rule, not just describe the parade? — C1.3 deepest evidence. The hundred-chart thumbnail is a scaffold, not a constraint — children may pick numbers entirely from it or invent their own (any 1–50). Children who write counting patterns (1, 2, 3, 4) instead of repeating patterns need a redirect — counting is Grade 2 territory.
